newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen up $0.50-$1.00 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen up $0.50-$1.00 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Tuesday were seen up $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt, lifted by light marketings as another winter storm slowly moves through the Midwest, followed by extreme cold, livestock dealers said.
The storm dumped up to six inches of snow in Iowa and southern Minnesota and glazed roads with ice in central and southern Missouri, Illinois, Indiana and Ohio.

Top prices for hogs delivered to plants in Iowa and southern Minnesota could range from $55.00 to $55.50. Illinois top prices at plants could span from $55.00-$55.50, possibly up to $56.00, the dealers said.
Indiana/Ohio top hog prices at the plant could range $54.00 to $54.50 if receipts remain light.
However, once the weather improves, cash hog prices could sink fast as packers operating under unprofitable margins, aggressively press for lower prices, the dealers said.
Packer margins slipped in the face of rising hog prices while pork demand has remained sluggish, they said.
"They (packers) just can't sell the meat high enough to offset the higher price of hogs," one Iowa hog buyer said.
A Sunday fire at Excel Corp's Ottumwa, Iowa pork plant will keep the plant closed at least until Tuesday.

However, the plant closing was not expected to have much impact on the cash hog market as long as Excel can ship hogs normally processed at Ottumwa to its plants in Marshall, Mo., and Beardstown, Ill, the dealers said.
